newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end lacklustre bourse trade lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares end lacklustre bourse trade lower.

text.p: German shares ended bourse dealings on Friday generally lower as Daimler-Benz AG took a beating after two major investment banks lowered earnings estimates on the industrial group.

The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 30.14 points at 4,408.79 points, with support for the index stabilising at 4,400 points. Support also came from the dollar trading at 1.84 marks, with 1.85 marks looking like a possibility.
Dealers expected the share market to remain under pressure over the rest of the day from profit-taking, particularly in the run-up to the release at 1230 GMT of U.S. July jobs data.

Market attention focused on Merill Lynch and Morgan Stanley downgrading 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for Daimler. Merrill also cut Daimler to intermediate reduce from neutral but left the share as a long-term hold.
The downgrades came after Daimler released six-month results that showed group operating profit more than doubling to 1.849 billion marks.
Daimler shares ended down 5.90 marks at 148.90 marks.
Daimler chief executive Juergen Schrempp said in a radio interview on Friday that he did not understand the disappointment among analysts.
"It is a excellent performance when a company more than doubles its operating profit," Schrempp told InfoRadio.
Some traders said the drop was an overreaction and ABN AMRO issued a buy recommendation on Daimler.
Other major DAX index components were lower, including banking industry shares such as Commerzbank AG and Deutsche Bank AG.
Commerzbank ended down 35 pfennigs at 62.65 marks, while Deutsche was down 2.35 marks at 122.15 marks.
